Deleting a scheduled workout used to leave a calendar entry nobody could
remove. One tool was added: the server now declares 110.

## The workout was gone, the calendar entry was not

Delete a workout that still had a date on the calendar, and the entry outlived
it. Garmin drops it from the calendar service — the Calendar page stops showing
it, and so does the API — but the Connect home page keeps offering it under
"Today's activities" as a planned workout. Opening it answers:

```
We were unable to process your request. Please try again later.
```

because the workout behind it no longer exists.

There is no way back. Every call on that schedule resolves the workout first:

```
DELETE /workout-service/schedule/{id}   404 No workout found for workout schedule = N
GET    /workout-service/schedule/{id}   404 No workout found for workout schedule = N
PUT    /workout-service/schedule/{id}   404 No workout found for workout schedule = N
```

Neither this server nor Garmin's own interface can take the entry off the home
page. It sits there until its date has passed.

## delete_workout clears the calendar first

`delete_workout` now reads the calendar, removes every **future** date of the
workout, and only then deletes it. The answer says which dates it freed:

```
Workout deleted successfully, after removing 2 scheduled date(s):
2026-09-15, 2027-06-01
```

If the calendar cannot be read, or a schedule refuses to go, **the workout is
not deleted** — a deletion worth retrying beats an entry that lasts for ever.
Past dates are left untouched: they are the record of what was planned.

## get_scheduled_workouts

A new read-only tool lists the workouts on the calendar in a date range, each
with the `workoutScheduleId` that `unschedule_workout` needs. With no arguments
it covers the next twelve months.

It was the missing half of scheduling. The workout service has no endpoint that
lists the schedules of a workout — every `/workout-service/workout/{id}/…` path
answers an empty array — and the calendar is the only place the id appears. Lose
the id returned by `schedule_workout`, and the date could not be freed again.

`unschedule_workout` also explains that 404 now instead of repeating it: Garmin
sends the same message for an id that never existed, one already unscheduled,
and one whose workout was deleted first.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.5.8...v4.5.9
